<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par142 />(''d'') ''Object—Subject—Verb'' (very rarely): {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=16}} (read {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}}).<ref>This sequence occurs more frequently in noun-clauses with a participial predicate, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=4}}, &c., in interrogative sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=19}}; in all which cases the emphasized object is placed before the natural sequence of ''subject—predicate''. [Cf. Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 208.]</ref>

(''e'') A substantival complement of the verb {{GHGheb|text=היה}} is placed first in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וּבֹסֵר גֹּמֵל יִֽהְיֶה נִצָּה|translate=and a ripening grape the flower becometh}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|142|g}}
Rem. Of specifications compounded with a preposition those of ''place'' stand regularly after the verb, unless they are specially emphatic as e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=12}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּרָחֵל}} with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} ''pretii'' precedes for the sake of emphasis. Cf., however, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=13}} the order {{GHGterm|verb}}—specification of ''place—subject''.—The remoter object precedes for the sake of emphasis, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=15}} (26:3), 15:3; even before the interrogative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=37}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=15}} where the subject precedes an interrogative, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=31}} where a prepositional specification precedes).—Prepositional specifications of ''time'', such as {{GHGheb|text=בְּרֵאשִׁית}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=1}}), {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא}}, &c. (but not {{GHGheb|text=בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָה}}, nor the simple {{GHGheb|text=רִֽאשֹׁנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּתְּחִלָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְעוֹלָם}}), stand, as a rule, before the verb, provided it be not in the perf. consec. or imperf. consec.; so also certain adverbs of time, such as {{GHGheb|text=אָז}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַתָּה}}, whilst others like {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּמִיד}} regularly follow the verb.<section end=par142 />

<section begin=par143 />{{GHGpar-heading|143|The Compound Sentence}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|143|a}}
A compound sentence ({{GHGpar|140|d}}) is formed by the juxtaposition of a subject<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=40}} a verbal-clause ({{GHGheb|text=הָיִ֫יתִי|translate=I was}}) occurs instead of the subject, and is then explained by another verbal-clause.</ref> (which always precedes, see ''c'') and

(''a'') An independent noun-clause, which (α) refers to the principal subject by means of a pronoun, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה בְּסוּפָה דַרְכּוֹ}} ''the Lord—in the storm is his way''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=125|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=14}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=23}}, where the predicate is an interrogative clause.—A personal pronoun is somewhat frequently used as the principal subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲנִי זֹאת בְּרִיתִי אֹתָם|translate=and as for me, this is my covenant with them}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=28|verse=2}};<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Chr|chapter=28|verse=2}} (cf. also 22:7 {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי הָיָה עִם־לְבָבִי}}) {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} might also be taken as strengthening the pronominal suffix which follows (equivalent to ''I myself had it in my mind''), as e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=17}} ''whereas their own way is not equal''; cf. {{GHGpar|135|f}}.</ref> with an interrogative noun-clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=19|hidebook=1}}:—or (β) is without a retrospective suffix (in which case naturally the connexion between the subject and predicate is much looser), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=23}} ''and'' as touching ''the matter which'', &c.... ''behold the Lord is between thee and me for ever''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=2}}.
<section end=par143 /><noinclude>
